questions.q: Why does this lesson recommend pinning dependencies with `==` instead of a loose range?
options: Loose ranges are not supported by pip
Pinning makes pip install run faster regardless of package size
Pinning is only relevant for web frameworks, not AI libraries
A minor version bump in a package like torch or transformers can silently change a model's numerical output
questions.explain: Exact pins (`==`) guarantee the same resolved versions every build, which matters more for AI libraries where a version change can change numerical behavior.

questions.q: What's the main downside of baking a large model checkpoint directly into an image with COPY?
options: It makes every build, push, and pull slower, and the registry stores a multi-gigabyte blob per image version
COPY cannot be used with files larger than 1MB
It requires a GPU to build
It automatically deletes the application code
questions.explain: Baked-in weights bloat the image, slowing the build/push/pull cycle and duplicating large blobs across image versions even when only the code changed.

questions.q: What's the key advantage of mounting model weights as a volume at runtime, instead of baking them in?
options: Volumes make the model run faster on GPU
The image stays small and generic, and weights become swappable without a rebuild
Volumes are required by Docker for any file over 10MB
It removes the need for a Dockerfile entirely
questions.explain: A volume-mounted model lives outside the image, so the same image can serve different model versions just by changing what's mounted.

questions.q: Per this lesson's guidance, which option fits a small, rarely-updated model under about 100MB?
options: Downloading it fresh on every build
Mounting it as a volume
Baking it directly into the image
Storing it in an environment variable
questions.explain: For small, stable models, the simplicity of a self-contained image outweighs the minor size cost — bake it in.

questions.q: If a team updates model weights weekly while the application code rarely changes, which approach avoids pushing a multi-gigabyte image to the registry every week?
options: Downloading the weights at build time on every single build
Baking the weights into the image on every release
Mounting the weights as a volume, so the image itself doesn't need to change when only the weights do
Storing the weights inside a .dockerignore file
questions.explain: Since the weights live outside the image under the volume approach, a weekly model update doesn't require rebuilding or re-pushing the (unchanged) image.
